title: SAR tomography detects King's Chamber, relieving chamber beams and 'sarcophagus'
summary: Jeffrey tells of SAR tomography detects King's Chamber, relieving chamber beams and 'sarcophagus', about 2020 at Egypt (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.
place_text: King's Chamber, Great Pyramid, Giza, Egypt

tellings.quote: Again, the red is indicating a very strong vibrational signature from inside of the structure.

related.note: Both are about whether the 2020 SAR scan of the Great Pyramid picks up the King's Chamber. The story says it shows no clear signature, while this telling says it detects the chamber, the beams and the sarcophagus.

plain: A researcher called Jeffrey, on Jesse Michels's podcast, describes a 2020 paper, credited to a scientist named Filippo, that used satellite radar to read vibrations inside the Great Pyramid of Giza. He says the scan picks up the King's Chamber, the main inner room, along with the stone beams above it and the stone box known as the sarcophagus, with red areas showing a very strong vibration signal from inside. If the method works as described, it could map hidden spaces inside the pyramid without digging.
